items.title: First-time setup
items.text:
The first time you open Fluidd (or Mainsail, or look at the touchscreen) after installing OpenCreator, a dialog welcomes you and asks four questions:

  • Pressure advance calibration: measure each tool's pressure advance over the purge bucket at the start of every print.
  • Purging: purge each tool into the bucket at the start of every print.
  • Clog Detection: pause the print when a tool's filament wheel stops turning while filament is still loaded in it. Off by default.
  • Bed heat soak: before a fresh bed mesh, wait a few minutes at bed temperature so the plate finishes warping first. Off by default.

Then it says where your tool offsets and dock positions come from and how to recalibrate them, and recommends recalibrating VFA compensation once.

There's nothing you have to calibrate first: a first install on the printer (SoC) takes your printer's own calibration from FlashForge's config (/usr/data/config/printer.cfg), so it starts with the input shaper and the PID tuning of all four hotends and the bed that FlashForge measured. The bed mesh isn't taken; OpenCreator measures its own. A reinstall or update keeps the config you already have. Tunneled installs start with the template's values, so calibrate those yourself.

To calibrate yourself anyway: CALIBRATE_INPUT_SHAPER (or CALIBRATE_INPUT_SHAPER_GRAPH for graphs too), VFA_COMPENSATION, and C5_PID_CALIBRATE TOOL=1 TARGET=250 for a heater (add TOLERANCE=0.1 if a noisy heater won't settle; the default is 0.05).

One calibration we do recommend running once, when you're ready: VFA compensation. OpenCreator's VFA calibration is much better than stock's, and the dialog has a page saying so.

The next page explains when to run the two other calibrations: C5_CALIBRATE_OFFSETS if the tools' offsets weren't right on the stock firmware either, and C5_CALIBRATE_TOOL_POSITION if a tool doesn't dock or pick up cleanly.

Fluidd also starts with the OpenCreator macro layout: the macros grouped into On / Off, Calibrations, Toolhead and Misc. A layout you already set up in Fluidd is kept.

If you close the dialog before finishing, it comes back within a minute. Once you reach the last page it won't appear again. Both choices are ordinary switches under Fans & Outputs, so you can change them at any time. To go through the dialog again, send C5_FIRST_SETUP in the console.

items.title: Camera streamer (experimental option)
items.text:
The camera streams with mjpg_streamer by default. ustreamer is available as an experimental alternative. It passes the camera's own MJPEG frames through with almost no CPU, copes better with several viewers or a slow connection, and skips repeated frames when nothing moves.

To switch, edit camera.conf in the config folder (Fluidd or Mainsail: Configuration), then restart the printer:

streamer: ustreamer

Switching to ustreamer needs Wi-Fi.

streamer: mjpg_streamer switches back. The camera keeps the same port, addresses and colour settings, so Fluidd, Mainsail and Timelapse need no changes. If ustreamer stops three times in a row within 30 seconds of starting, the printer goes back to mjpg_streamer until the next restart, and says so in /tmp/opencreator.log. ustreamer's own log is /usr/data/logs/ustreamer.log.

items.title: Screen timeout
items.text:
The touchscreen's backlight turns off after 5 minutes without a touch, and on again at the next touch. That waking touch doesn't press anything. A keyboard or gamepad on the printer's USB keeps it on too, and so does Sonic Mania or DOOM while you play.

To change the time, edit screen-timeout.conf in the config folder from Fluidd or Mainsail: timeout: 300 is in seconds, and 0 keeps the screen on. The change takes effect within a few seconds.

It runs as its own small service beside the screen app, so it works with GrumpyScreen and HelixScreen alike.

items.title: Timelapse
items.text:
The OpenCreator Installer sets up Moonraker Timelapse. It takes a camera frame at every layer change and renders them into an MP4 when the print finishes. The videos show up under Timelapse in Fluidd and Mainsail, where you can also change its settings (frame rate, parking the toolhead for each frame, and so on).

To record a print, add TIMELAPSE_TAKE_FRAME to the slicer's layer change G-code (see Slicer Configuration). Without it, only hyperlapse mode records, which takes frames at a fixed interval instead.

Printer (SoC) Raspberry Pi (tunnel) Camera The printer camera, through its snapshot URL The webcam you set up in Fluidd or Mainsail ffmpeg FlashForge's own build, already on the printer Installed from apt Frames /usr/data/opencreator/timelapse/frames/ /tmp/timelapse/ Videos /usr/data/opencreator/timelapse/ ~/printer_data/timelapse/

Rendering on the printer

On the printer, ffmpeg runs at the lowest priority so it never holds up Klipper, which makes rendering slow: expect a few minutes for a long print. Frames are kept on storage rather than in /tmp, which is RAM and too small for a long print.

Moonraker's update manager keeps Timelapse current, as the timelapse entry.

items.title: Input shaper graphs
items.text:
CALIBRATE_INPUT_SHAPER_GRAPH does the same as CALIBRATE_INPUT_SHAPER (measures both axes, applies the recommended shaper and saves it; add SAVE=0 to save later), and also draws a graph of each axis on the printer, the same graph Klipper's calibrate_shaper.py makes on a PC. It is under Calibrations on Fluidd's Macros card (Uncategorized on installs whose macro layout is older than the macro).

The graphs are saved to the config folder as input_shaper/shaper_x.png and input_shaper/shaper_y.png; open them from the config files in Fluidd or Mainsail.

  • Left axis: the measured vibrations (X, Y, Z and their sum) at each frequency. Peaks are resonances; After shaper is what the recommended shaper leaves of them.
  • Right axis: how much each shaper lets through at each frequency. The recommended shaper is dash-dotted; the legend gives each one's frequency, remaining vibrations, smoothing and the highest acceleration it suits.

The figures come from Kalico's own shaper code, so they match what SHAPER_CALIBRATE reports in the console.

items.title: Flow Calibration in the Creator 5 factory firmware
items.text:
The touchscreen calls this Flow Calibration, but the routine is intended to test pressure advance. It does not measure a printed line's width, weigh extruded plastic, or calculate an extrusion multiplier. The host tries several pressure-advance values while the eboard observes the extruder motor driver's SG_RESULT load signal. The eboard reports whether each sampled waveform passes its check.

The sequence below is reconstructed from the factory firmwareExe.i64 database, principally BuildPage::clearNozzlePrint and CommMgr::paTestMgr, and from the factory eBoard.hex.

items.title: The stock test, step by step
items.text:
1. The host resets the extruder position with G92 E0, switches to relative extrusion with M83, sets acceleration to 5000 mm/s² and square-corner velocity to 9 mm/s, enables the X/Y motor-driver control pins, and waits for queued motion to finish.
  2. It tries these pressure-advance candidates in this order: 0.0100, 0.0200, 0.0150, 0.0350, 0.0250, 0.0300, and 0.0400. For each candidate it sends PA_ACTION ACTION=11 PC=666 to arm the eboard measurement, then SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE ADVANCE=<candidate>.
  3. The carriage starts each candidate at X40 and a Y position from 50 to 80 in 5 mm steps. It extrudes across six X strokes ending at X60, X100, X120, X140, X180, and X200. The X and Y movements don't actually happen and get discarded, this is mostly to trick Klippy into thinking PA can be used. The short strokes extrude 1.13573 mm of filament at F1080 (18 mm/s); the long strokes extrude 2.27146 mm at F10980 (183 mm/s). Alternating slow and fast motion creates the motor-load transient that the eboard examines.
  4. The host sends PA_ACTION ACTION=0 PC=666, waits with M400, and reads PA_GET. It treats a returned value of 9 as a pass for that candidate.

The eboard firmware's pa_action handler resets its result and sample area when action 11 starts a measurement, switches its acquisition mode, then finalizes the capture when action 0 arrives. get_emcu_pa_value reports the result back to the host as pa_value value=<number>. 9 means "pass"; it isn't the measured pressure advance. How the eboard decides is described below. The host always sends PC=666, and what that value means isn't known yet.

items.title: Where the waveform comes from
items.text:
The host does not synthesize an electrical waveform. It commands a sequence of extruder moves. Changing extrusion speed changes the motor's mechanical load; the TMC2209 turns that load into successive SG_RESULT register values. The eboard reads those values over UART and stores valid replies in time order. Plotting sample index against SG_RESULT produces the waveform that the classifier examines. Consecutive samples are roughly 2 ms apart when no reply is lost; dropped replies make sample index an imperfect time axis. It is a driver load estimate, not a direct motor current measurement or a measurement of deposited plastic.

In the current OpenCreator/Kalico bucket test, the carriage stays at the purge bucket while E alone runs through six relative extrusion moves:

Segment Filament commanded Default E speed Nominal time at speed Slow 1.13573 mm 4.5 mm/s 252 ms Fast 2.27146 mm 22.875 mm/s 99 ms Slow 1.13573 mm 4.5 mm/s 252 ms Slow 1.13573 mm 4.5 mm/s 252 ms Fast 2.27146 mm 22.875 mm/s 99 ms Slow 1.13573 mm 4.5 mm/s 252 ms

Those durations are distance divided by speed, not exact captured pulse widths: acceleration, motion planning, and transitions between moves alter the actual timing. The test commands 9.08584 mm of filament per candidate. PA_ACTION ACTION=11 starts sampling before the moves; M400 drains them, and PA_ACTION ACTION=0 closes the capture. The eboard polls the driver about every 2 ms, accepts only complete replies with a valid CRC, and reserves 2,000 sample slots (about four seconds). Missing or invalid replies are not valid load observations.

Current limitation: Kalico's extruder planner applies pressure advance only when an extrusion move also has X or Y travel. These bucket strokes are E-only, so changing SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE between candidates does not itself reshape their E motion. A pass currently shows that the driver-load waveform matches the eboard's stroke criteria; it does not prove that the selected pressure-advance value is optimal. The factory routine issues XY/E strokes, whereas the current bucket-safe port intentionally omits XY movement. The stock firmware's full waveform and its PA discrimination have not been established by this Kalico implementation alone.

items.title: How the eboard judges a stroke
items.text:
This is how OpenCreator's own eboard firmware (in Kalico, src/c5_eboard_pa.c) does it.

Sampling. While a measurement runs, the eboard asks the extruder's TMC2209 driver for its load reading (SG_RESULT) about every 2 ms, roughly 500 times a second. The response parser checks its framing and CRC before storing a reading.

Judging. In those readings the eboard looks for a stroke:

  1. Start: the reading climbs by more than 99 without dropping.
  2. End: the reading stays at 70 or below for 0.4 s (or the readings run out).
  3. Plateau: the part above 150, minus 60 ms at each end.

The stroke passes when all of these are true:

  • The plateau averages more than 150.
  • The plateau lasts about 160–300 ms, roughly one slow stroke.
  • Early in the stroke the reading jumps more than 20% above the plateau, for at least 3 readings.
  • At the end it drops cleanly, from between half and all of the plateau level down to near zero.

If any stroke passes, the eboard answers 9.

items.title: What can make it fail
items.text:
• Klipper talking to the same driver. Klipper checks the extruder driver about once a second over the same wire, which garbles the eboard's readings and stops the test from ever passing. OpenCreator's flow test now pauses those checks while it runs.
  • No X/Y motion. Klipper only applies pressure advance to moves that include X or Y motion, so extruding in place tests nothing. Like the stock firmware, OpenCreator runs the stock X/Y strokes, but with the X/Y motors held still: they stay powered and locked, they just aren't sent any steps. The nozzle stays over the bucket, and afterwards the printer knows exactly where it is again, so no re-homing is needed.
  • Driver mode. The TMC2209 only gives a useful SG_RESULT in its quiet StealthChop mode, so OpenCreator runs the extruder driver in StealthChop (stealthchop_threshold: 999999 on [tmc2209 extruder] to [tmc2209 extruder3]). Klipper's default would be SpreadCycle. On stock firmware the eboard sets up the driver itself, so the stock config has no driver settings to compare with.

To see the driver settings the stock eboard uses, run DUMP_TMC STEPPER=extruder in the console of a printer still on stock firmware.

items.title: How it chooses and applies a result
items.text:
One pass tests up to seven candidates and keeps the smallest candidate for which the eboard returned 9. The host allows up to five passes, stopping once three passes produce a valid candidate. It averages those three selected values to produce that tool's result. If fewer than three passes succeed, the test reports failure rather than producing a new value. The routine also cleans up its motor-driver test mode after completion or interruption.

After preparing the tools, the print-start code sends SET_PA_ADVANCE with the successful T0–T3 results and ENABLE=1. Entries without a result are filled with 99.0 as placeholders. If flow testing is off, or no valid tool result is available, it sends SET_PA_ADVANCE T0=99.0 T1=99.0 T2=99.0 T3=99.0 ENABLE=0. These final per-tool settings are distinct from the temporary SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE candidate applied during each test.

items.title: Host pressure-advance test (OpenCreator, experimental)
items.text:
C5_FLOW_STROKES METHOD=host is OpenCreator's own pressure-advance test. The stock test only says whether each fixed candidate passes or fails. This one has Klippy look at every driver reading itself and work out the pressure advance, so it isn't limited to the stock candidates. It takes about a minute per tool, where the stock test takes about two and a half.

It needs OpenCreator's eboard firmware with the reading stream (flashed by installer 0.4.8 and later), and StealthChop on the extruder drivers, the same as the stock test.

At print start it runs when the host_pressure_advance switch is on (Fans & Outputs, C5_MISC_HOST_PRESSURE_ADVANCE_ON/_OFF, or HOST_PRESSURE_ADVANCE=1 on C5_PRINT_START), with APPLY=1. It is off by default and separate from the stock flow_calibration switch. With both on, the stock test runs first and the host test after it; if the host result is rejected, the stock value stays.

items.title: The idea
items.text:
Pressure advance models nozzle pressure as trailing the extruder motor. The right advance is the one that cancels that lag: by the time the motor reaches a steady speed, pressure has already caught up.

So the test runs the extruder fast at a constant speed and watches the motor's load (SG_RESULT) during that steady part:

  • Too little advance: pressure is still building, so the load keeps rising.
  • Too much advance: the extra push overshoots, so the load falls back.
  • Right advance: the load stays flat.

Because the motor speed isn't changing during that part, a change in load can only come from the melt pressure. The test measures this drift at a few advance values and finds where it crosses zero.

items.title: Readings
items.text:
The stock eboard firmware only keeps its readings to make its own pass/fail decision. OpenCreator's eboard firmware also keeps each reading with the eboard's clock time, and Klippy downloads them afterwards (get_pa_stream). That's about 500 readings a second, up to 6,000 (12 s) per run. Each one is matched to the extruder's commanded position and speed at that moment.

Without that firmware, SENSOR=sg has Klippy poll the driver itself instead, which gives far fewer readings.

items.title: The strokes
items.text: Each run starts with 0.4 s at 1 mm/s of filament, then six strokes. Each stroke is 0.5 s at 10.4 mm/s, then 0.4 s back at 1 mm/s. As in the stock test, the X/Y motors are held still, and each move has X/Y travel four times its extrusion so Klipper applies pressure advance to it. The first stroke is only a warm-up and isn't scored.

items.title: Scoring a stroke
items.text:
Every stroke is measured from the moment it reaches speed:

  • Early: 0.03–0.09 s in, just after the advance's own push has finished.
  • Late: the rest of the stroke, up to 0.02 s before it ends.

The stroke's drift is (early − late) / late.

The motor's load reading also ripples with each electrical cycle of the motor: once every four full steps, which is 0.0589 mm of filament on these extruders. That ripple was more than half of the reading noise during a stroke. The test fits it across all of a run's strokes (four harmonics) and removes it before it compares early and late.

items.title: Finding the answer
items.text:
1. The test runs at advances of 0, 0.05 and 0.10, which gives 15 scored strokes.
  2. It fits a straight line through (advance, drift) and takes the advance where the line crosses zero. A stroke whose reading drops to 0 or near it stalled the motor and isn't used.
  3. Now and then a stroke reads far off. Up to a tenth of the strokes that sit more than four robust standard deviations off the line are dropped, and the line is fitted again.
  4. If the load barely responds (|t| below 4), the test runs the same advances again, up to 24 runs in all. PLA needs this: its pressure settles within about 20 ms, so each stroke shows only a small drift.
  5. The fit gives a 95% range for the answer. If that range is wider than 0.03, the test runs twice more, at the answer ±0.01. It repeats this until the range is narrow enough, or until it has used six runs on this, the same as a normal nine-run test.

The answer is rejected, and nothing is changed, when:

Reason Meaning Load does not respond The drift barely changes with advance (|t| below 4). Usually the driver isn't in StealthChop. Drifts the wrong way Drift rises with advance, the opposite of what pressure does. Outside the tested range The answer is more than 0.02 outside the advances that were tested. Too uncertain The 95% range is still wider than 0.03 after nine runs.

The trace is written to /tmp/c5_flow_T<tool>.csv (one row per reading: run, advance, time, filament position, reading, commanded speed and acceleration). The console shows each stroke's drift and the result, for example:

T2 host flow test: pressure advance 0.0751 (95%: 0.0633-0.0869, t=-6.3, 25 strokes, 5 runs)

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
Parameter Default APPLY 0 1 sets the result as the tool's pressure advance if it isn't rejected ADVANCES 0,0.05,0.10 Advances for the first runs, comma separated REFINE 1 0 skips the extra runs MAX_RUNS 9 Limit on runs, including the extra ones WEAK_RUNS 24 Limit on runs when the load barely responds; 0 turns the repeats off CURRENT 1 Experimental: extruder run current during the strokes, as a fraction of the configured one. Lower makes pressure show up more, but noise grows as fast. Below about 0.8 the advance's push stalls the motor: on PETG this left too few strokes at PA 0.10 and gave 0.058 instead of about 0.075. SENSOR eboard eboard: the eboard's reading stream; sg: Klippy polls the driver (used when the eboard firmware has no stream) FAST 10.4 Stroke speed, mm/s of filament SLOW 1 Speed between strokes, mm/s of filament STROKES 6 Strokes per run FAST_TIME 0.5 Stroke length, s SLOW_TIME 0.4 Time between strokes, s LEAD 0.4 Slow time before the first stroke, s RATIO 0.25 Filament per mm of the (held) X/Y travel

The tool must be attached and at printing temperature, with Z calibrated, as for the stock test.

items.title: Results so far
items.text:
On T2 with PETG at 255 °C, five runs gave 0.067, 0.068, 0.074, 0.075 and 0.079 (one of these was rejected as too uncertain, before the extra runs were added). The others took under a minute each. The stock test gives 0.028–0.030 for the same filament.

The stock test is limited by the motion more than by the filament. Its end check fails above about 0.037 because the retract outruns the stroke's own speed, and its spike check needs at least about 0.02. That leaves about 0.03 for most filaments.

Neither number has been checked against a print yet, so leave APPLY at 0 until it has. To check, print a pressure-advance tower with the same filament:

TUNING_TOWER COMMAND=SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE PARAMETER=ADVANCE START=0 FACTOR=.005

Then compare the height where the corners look best with both results.

items.title: Filament dryer (VDS)
items.text:
On the SoC install, OpenCreator drives FlashForge's two-chamber VDS filament dryer the same way the stock firmware does: over the printer's internal serial port /dev/ttyS3 at 115200 baud. Plug the dryer in where FlashForge says to before installing: the installer only turns the dryer controls on when a dryer answers. It then writes printer.accessory.dryer.cfg, which loads printer.dryer.cfg. If you add a dryer later, rerun the installer or add [include printer.dryer.cfg] to printer.cfg yourself.

Command What it does C5_DRYER_START CHAMBER=A\|B\|AB TEMP=45-85 HOURS=1-48 Dry one or both chambers (MINUTES=60-2880 works instead of HOURS) C5_DRYER_STOP CHAMBER=A\|B\|AB Stop drying C5_DRYER_PAUSE CHAMBER=A\|B\|AB Turn the heaters off; start again with C5_DRYER_START C5_DRYER_DEHUMIDIFY CHAMBER=A\|B\|AB ENABLE=0\|1 Keep a chamber dry after drying C5_DRYER_STATUS Firmware version, and each chamber's state, temperature, humidity and time left C5_DRYER_PLA, C5_DRYER_PETG, C5_DRYER_ABS, C5_DRYER_OFF Presets (50, 65 and 80 °C for 6 hours) and stop; add CHAMBER=A or B for one chamber

CHAMBER defaults to both. The chambers also show up as the temperature sensors dryer_a and dryer_b, with their humidity, so Fluidd and Mainsail graph them. Macros can read printer.creator5_dryer (connected, firmware_version, and per chamber drying, temperature, humidity, remaining_minutes).

The dryer's own firmware limits drying to 45-85 °C and 1-48 hours. OpenCreator doesn't update the dryer's firmware; if C5_DRYER_STATUS says it is in its bootloader, update it from stock FlashForge firmware.

items.title: Offset Calibration
items.text:
Offset calibration aligns the nozzles of T0–T3 for printing. It is separate from locating their docks. The Creator 5 port exposes it through C5_CALIBRATE_OFFSETS; measurements and the levelboard reference are kept in /usr/data/firmwareRes/config/extruder.json.

Calibration cannot run during a print. If a tool is attached, the carriage first raises it to the safe Z clearance and docks it. The ordinary calibration pin is then probed at two known locations. Their contact-height difference is used to reject a plate that may still be installed and to set a safe approach floor for the following measurements.

With the carriage bare, the routine contacts the levelboard fixture to establish its Z reference, then scans outward from its center for the X+, Y+, X-, and Y- edges. Each edge scan is limited to 7 mm; opposite edges give the fixture's X/Y center. The routine then picks up T0, probes its Z against the fixture, scans its four X/Y edges, raises clear of the fixture, and docks it. It repeats that sequence for T1, T2, and T3. The saved X/Y printing offsets are each tool's measured center relative to T0. Its nozzle Z offset uses the tool's measured Z relative to the fixture reference, plus the separate per-tool Z fine adjustment. The code rejects measurements beyond its configured correction limits or an unsafe resulting nozzle Z offset.

CFW

The all-tool run saves only after all four tools succeed. It makes a backup of extruder.json and replaces that file atomically, so a failed tool does not leave a partially saved set. The measured offsets are also applied to the active tool through Klipper's G-code offset when it is selected.

A single tool can be recalibrated with TOOL=0 through TOOL=3. It still requires removing and checking the build plate; it docks any attached tool, checks the ordinary pin, and automatically picks up the requested tool. LEVELBOARD=0 skips refreshing the bare fixture reference for a single tool, but does not skip that tool's levelboard measurement. Z=0 performs XY-only calibration and needs a configured scan height or SCAN_Z; the default Z=1 probes the nozzle Z automatically. TOOL=ALL always refreshes the fixture reference and requires Z=1.

items.title: Baby stepping
items.text:
Baby stepping a tool's Z offset during a print, from Fluidd's or Mainsail's Z adjust buttons or SET_GCODE_OFFSET Z_ADJUST=, is saved as you go. It's saved as that tool's Z adjustment in /usr/data/firmwareRes/config/zoffset.json, the same value the touchscreen's Z offset sets. Each nozzle keeps its own value: a step goes to whichever head is attached. The next print, and the same nozzle after a toolchange, start from it, read from that file each time, so it's kept across restarts too.

Macro What it does LIST_BABYSTEP Shows the saved Z adjustment for every tool. TOOL=2 shows only T2. CLEAR_BABYSTEP TOOL=1 Resets T1's saved Z adjustment to 0. With no TOOL, or TOOL=ALL, it resets all four.

Clearing the attached tool also takes the adjustment off its current Z offset. Because the touchscreen uses the same value, clearing a tool also clears its touchscreen Z offset.

A Z change of more than 1 mm at once isn't treated as baby stepping and isn't saved. To stop saving baby stepping, add persist_babystep: False to [creator5_toolchanger].

items.title: Toolhead Dock Calibration
items.text:
Toolhead dock calibration, called Extruder Position Calibrate in the factory UI, finds the physical pickup/docking X/Y coordinates for one tool. It does not change the nozzle offsets used to align layers during a print. In the Creator 5 port, run C5_CALIBRATE_TOOL_POSITION T=0 through T=3, or use the underlying EXTRUDER_POSITION_CALIBRATE T=n command.

Before starting, park all four tools, home the printer, raise Z to at least the configured safe clearance (10 mm in the supplied config), and let every toolhead cool below 50 °C. A print must not be active. The build plate does not need to be removed for this calibration.

  1. The routine disables X/Y motors and asks you to move the bare master carriage by hand to the chosen parked tool. It waits for both that dock's holder sensor and its grab sensor to register contact.
  2. Once contact is detected, it asks you to release the carriage and waits briefly before taking over. It latches the tool and pulls it clear, checking that the holder sensor released while the grab sensor remains active.
  3. It measures X and Y against the printer's X/Y home references, calculates the dock coordinates, and rejects a correction beyond the configured limit (2 mm in the supplied config).
  4. It rehomes X/Y, redocks the tool using the measured coordinates, and only then saves them as x_check_pos/y_check_pos for T0, or the corresponding numbered keys for T1–T3, in extruder.json. A timestamped backup is made first.

If contact, sensor verification, measurement, or redocking fails, the routine does not save new dock coordinates.

items.title: Mainboard and power supply fans
items.text:
The mainboard has two fans of its own: one cooling the board and the X/Y/Z motor drivers, and one in the power supply. Stock runs both at full speed whenever the motors are powered or a hotend is heating. OpenCreator only runs them as fast as the printer needs, so they are much quieter most of the time.

  • Mainboard fan: follows the mainboard chip's own temperature. Off below 54.5 °C, from 30% at 54.5 °C up to full speed at 65 °C, and at least 40% while the motors are powered, for the drivers.
  • Power supply fan: follows the power supply's estimated load, from the hotends' heater power and the motors. 30% at light load, at least 50% while a hotend is heating, full speed at about 120 W. It never runs slower than the mainboard fan. Once the load is gone it keeps running for a minute at most 80%, then stops.

Both ramp up and down smoothly instead of switching between off and full. They are checked every second on their own timer, so long commands such as PID calibration, heat-up waits or homing don't stop them.

During input shaper, VFA and ripple calibration both fans are held at 50%, so their vibration stays the same through the measurement.

C5_BOARD_FANS shows both speeds, the mainboard temperature and the estimated load. C5_BOARD_FANS HOLD=0.5 holds both fans at 50% (HOLD=-1 releases them), and any setting can be changed until the next restart, e.g. C5_BOARD_FANS MAX_TEMP=65. To keep a change, edit [c5_board_fans] in printer.base.cfg.

items.title: MCU temperatures
items.text: Fluidd and Mainsail show the temperature of the mainboard chip (mainboard_mcu) and of the toolhead board's chip (toolhead_mcu). They are only for keeping an eye on things; the mainboard one also drives the mainboard fan.

items.title: Motion guard
items.text: The motion guard watches the X, Y and Z motors for skipped steps and stalls during a print, from the mainboard's own motor control. It is off by default, as it reported too many false alarms while the motors were crawling or holding still. C5_MOTION_GUARD ENABLE=1 turns it on until the next restart (ACTION=pause to pause the print instead of warning), and C5_MOTION_STATUS shows what it has counted.

items.title: SBC Installation and Configuration
items.text:
SBC / RPI Klipper for replacing the Mips32 Host that comes with the printer. The printer's own board keeps only a serial bridge that forwards its four MCUs to the SBC over one USB cable. Klipper, Moonraker and Fluidd run on the SBC.

flowchart LR
  subgraph SBC["SBC (Raspberry Pi or similar)"]
    K[Kalico / Klipper] --- M[Moonraker] --- F[Fluidd]
  end
  subgraph P["Creator 5 SoC"]
    B[c5-tunnel bridge]
  end
  SBC <-->|USB gadget, 4-5 serial ports| B
  B --- MB[mainBoardGD]
  B --- HB[heaterBoard]
  B --- EB[eBoard]
  B --- LB[levelBoard]

items.title: Reasons to go OpenCreator SBC over stock
items.text:
• More power

    Run fun projects, add more cameras, add monitoring with AI, etc.

  • Faster toolchanges

    Toolchanges are half a second to a second faster, since Klipper runs on the SBC's much faster CPU instead of the printer's.

  • Security

    Airgap the printer's old kernel version and potentially insecure packages, so they are only reached through the SBC.

  • Your choice of touchscreen

    Use different touchscreen apps, such as KlipperScreen instead of GrumpyScreen.

  • Standard tooling

    Use KIAUH to install utilities instead of manually, run ShakeTune natively, and have all the support of a good architecture.

items.title: What is the reason for development?
items.text:
On the stock system, you have amazing MCUs, but the worst SOCs, to the point of encountering issues. That wouldn't be normally an issue, manufacturers would put the minimum spec SOC, but FlashForge demanded too much for how slow and not powerful the stock SOC is (Ingenic x2600). It frequently runs into weirdness: even completely stock, with the stock touchscreen, you can't really print too fast with toolchanges and no prime tower, as it will hit Timer Too Close, which happens when the host (the SOC) can't catch up and falls behind. On 1.9.9 they even forced it to slow down to prevent this.

On OpenCreator SBC, Timer Too Close becomes a thing of the past, and you can run almost anything, as you're running on a Raspberry Pi or similar microcomputer that has several times the power of the stock board.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• A SBC that has USB Gadget Mode support (Pi Zero 2 W, Pi 4/5 on its USB-C power port, etc)
  • If using an external power supply on a Pi 4/5, a USB power and data splitter
  • If using an external power supply on a Pi 4/5, a USB-A power blocker for the USB data in/out port on the splitter
  • A recent Debian / Raspberry Pi OS Lite with up-to-date packages (headless / server installs recommended)
  • If running a slow device (1 GHz Pi Zero 2 W), an overclock to 1.2 GHz or above
  • Some type of cooling
  • At least 4GB of storage
  • At least 512MB of RAM
  • Internet on at least the SBC

items.title: Caveats
items.text:
Camera

The camera will not work if you airgap the MCUs. You will have to make a custom connector or add your own camera (in testing to rectify). The camera may also slow down during fast movements due to the USB bus being overloaded; if that persists it may need to be restarted.

Cables

A USB to spec cable is recommended, and as short as possible to keep signal integrity. Even if a cable looks good, that doesn't mean it actually is.

Wi-Fi on the printer

Unplugging / restarting the Pi causes the FlashForge printer's SoC to disconnect from Wi-Fi. It selects the virtual interface as internet and dies when it loses it.

No FlashForge integration

Obviously, no FlashForge cloud or app integration at all.

4 or 5 tunnel ports

The USB gadget tunnel normally runs 5 ports (4 MCUs + a dedicated beep channel). Not every board's USB controller tolerates this under sustained traffic: it is confirmed stable on a Raspberry Pi 4 (dwc2), but an Orange Pi Zero 2W's own controller destabilized the whole bus, and was stable at 4.

The gadget script falls back to 4 ports automatically if the 5-port bind fails outright at boot, and pins that choice for future boots. A failure that only shows up at runtime isn't detectable that way and still needs a manual pin:

echo 4 | sudo tee /etc/c5-tunnel-ports

Pinned to 4 ports, C5_BUZZER can optionally fall back to sending the beep over the network instead of going silent; see network_host in [creator5_remote_beeper].

items.title: On the printer
items.text:
1. Make sure the printer is on FlashForge firmware 1.9.9, then plug in the OpenCreator Installer media as outlined on the installation page
  2. Click to use "Tunneled", and choose whether to install the GrumpyScreen touchscreen
  3. Wait for installation to finish. The printer needs internet: it installs Entware, LoopScript and the socat bridge (details)
  4. Restart your printer
  5. If you installed GrumpyScreen, it opens up for a Moonraker printer. Edit /usr/data/grumpyscreen/grumpyscreen.cfg and set host: under [moonraker] to your Pi's IP address

items.title: On the SBC
items.text:
1. Plug in the SBC through the Gadget Mode port (USB-C on RPi 4/5, power micro USB for Zero 2 W).
  2. Install the software:
Automatic (recommended)Manual

As your normal user (not root):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlashForge-C5-Modding-Group/opencreator-tunnel/main/pi/install.sh | sh

This installs, in order: the tunnel repository, Fluidd, Moonraker, Kalico, the printer config, the OpenCreator Updater and the USB gadget service. An existing printer.cfg is left alone. On a first install, reboot afterwards so the USB gadget comes up.

  1. Set up Klipper (or Kalico), Moonraker, and Fluidd/Mainsail (Fluidd recommended).
  2. Clone opencreator-tunnel.
  3. Run sudo sh pi/setup-gadget.sh to install the gadget service if on RPi 3B+, 4, 5 or Zero 2 W. On another SBC, set up a gadget tunnel based on that service.
  4. Copy the configs from pi/config into ~/printer_data/config (plus pi/kalico if you use Kalico).
  5. Reboot, then restart the firmware for Klipper. It should connect if you did the printer first.

items.title: OpenCreator Updater
items.text:
An "opencreator-updater" entry in Fluidd's update manager. One click pulls the latest config and Klipper, and merges config changes into yours without overwriting values you customized. A change that conflicts with yours is written next to the file as <file>.conflict for you to look at, never into the live config.

Fluidd says \"No git repo detected\" for opencreator-updater

Run the repair script as your normal user:

sh ~/opencreator-tunnel/pi/opencreator-updater/repair.sh

It works wherever the repository is, starts git in a copied folder that has none, syncs to the official main branch (local edits are stashed, not deleted), fixes the moonraker.conf section and restarts Moonraker.

items.title: 3MF uploads
items.text: Sliced 3MF files (OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio "Export plate sliced file", .gcode.3mf) can be uploaded straight to Fluidd or from the slicer. The first sliced plate is extracted as G-code with its preview thumbnail. A 3MF with no sliced G-code is rejected.

items.title: OpenCreator Fluidd theme
items.text: An extra-dark Fluidd theme with the OpenCreator logo and orange accents is installed into ~/printer_data/config/.fluidd-theme/. It is made for Fluidd's dark mode. To go back to stock Fluidd, delete or rename .fluidd-theme/custom.css and reload the page.

items.title: Kalico
items.text: SBC installs run Kalico, which adds MPC heater control (C5_MPC_CALIBRATE) on top of everything the Klipper port does.

items.title: Extra notes
items.text:
The touchscreen might feel physically slow no matter the device unless you use GrumpyScreen or similar running locally on the printer itself. Streaming KlipperScreen to the printer's own screen over VNC (instead of running GrumpyScreen) was attempted but is not currently working: a second, isolated headless KlipperScreen instance (matched to the printer panel's resolution, so the VNC feed needs no scaling) hangs indefinitely during its own window setup under cage's headless Wayland backend, for reasons not yet root-caused. GrumpyScreen remains the supported local touchscreen option.

This could be fixed by using a touchscreen out from the SBC, such as something like this.

items.text: A collection of configurations and settings for Custom Firmware OpenCreator.

items.title: New - OrcaSlicer Cloud Profile
items.text: For those who do not want to do this manually, we now have an Orca Cloud Profile! Check it out here

items.title: OrcaSlicer Plugin
items.text: For those who want to replicate FlashForge's send dialogs, you can now use our OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 plugin! Just set it as a slicer pipeline plugin. Check it out here

items.title: Print profile
items.text:
• Under Quality → Precision, switch Arc fitting off.

    This improves performance with no quality loss, as arcs are not supported under Klipper.

  • Under Others → G-code output, switch Label objects and Exclude objects on.

    This lets adaptive bed meshing work correctly, and lets you exclude objects from the touchscreen and Fluidd/Mainsail.

items.title: Printer profile
items.text: These will change stuff like printer agents.

items.title: Connection
items.text:
• Click the Wi-Fi connect button (next to the printer) and change the host type to Moonraker.
  • Remove any serial numbers or API keys.

items.title: Printer settings
items.text:
• Printer Agent: switch to Moonraker.
  • Use 3MF instead of G-code: switch from on to off.
  • Disable set remaining print time: off.

3MFs

.gcode.3mf files will get automatically changed to normal .gcode on upload, so to optimize file size uploading, you may use it. This has a downside of unzip / parse time being much higher, but the time you save via internet uploading could be worth it.

items.title: Machine G-code
items.text:
• File header G-code: clear it (leave it empty). The FlashForge profile puts a FlashForge-style time estimate there, and Orca also copies that setting into the end of the file, where Moonraker reads it instead of the real estimate. With it in place, Fluidd and Mainsail show no slicer time estimate.

Files sliced before the change

OpenCreator's Moonraker component works around this for files uploaded from now on. Files already on the printer show no estimate until you upload them again.

  • Set your start G-Code to this:
;start_gcode
SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO TOTAL_LAYER=[total_layer_count]
M140 S[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single]
M191 S[overall_chamber_temperature]
M106 
M106 P2 S0 ; Center_Fresh_Air_Input_Fan_for_PLA30%_(80_0-255)
M106 S0 ; Model_Fan_(Heat_Break_Cooler_80-255)100%=255
M106 P3 S0 ; Filter_Unit_Fan_0-255(ABS=255)
G90
M83
;start_gcode end

  • Remove or comment out some G-code Print End (Newer versions of the profile): G1 X150 Y150 E-1.2 F12000

  • Layer change G-code (optional, for timelapses): add TIMELAPSE_TAKE_FRAME on its own line, so Timelapse takes a frame at every layer.

items.title: Optional / niceties
items.text:
Faster retractions

Set retraction and deretraction speed to 45 on all extruders. It should make it much faster, and doesn't seem to cause much stringing.

Lower Z-hop

Set Z-hop height to 0.3 on all extruders. It reduces stress on the Z axis and makes your prints slightly faster.

items.title: How to toggle features
items.text: Most OpenCreator CFW features are switches you can turn on or off, they are virtual switches that print start, print end and the rest of the firmware check. Each one keeps its setting across Klipper restarts and reboots.

items.title: Ways to change a switch
items.text:
FluiddMainsailMacrosConsole

Open the dashboard and find the Fans & Outputs card. Every switch is listed there by name.

The switches are on the dashboard under Miscellaneous.

Each switch has a pair of macros, for example C5_MISC_PURGE_ON and C5_MISC_PURGE_OFF. In Fluidd they are grouped under Misc on the Macros card. They print every switch's state when they finish.

Any switch can be set from the console with SET_PIN:

SET_PIN PIN=purge_line VALUE=0

C5_MISC lists the state of every switch.

items.title: Switches
items.text: Switch Default Macros What it does flow_calibration On C5_MISC_FLOW_CALIBRATION_ON / _OFF FlashForge PA calibration, known to be extremely inaccurate. Recommended off on first setup. purge On C5_MISC_PURGE_ON / _OFF Purges each prepared tool into the bucket at print start. With this and flow calibration both off, tool preparation is skipped. purge_line On C5_MISC_PURGE_LINE_ON / _OFF The purge line drawn in front of the print, just before it starts. Separate from purge. purge_line_all_tools Off C5_MISC_PURGE_LINE_ALL_TOOLS_ON / _OFF With purge_line on, every tool the print uses draws its own purge line at its own temperature, not only the first. Needs Kalico. See Print Workflow. bed_leveling On C5_MISC_BED_LEVEL_ON / _OFF Probes a fresh bed mesh before each print. Uses KAMP if slicer settings are correct. Off loads the saved default mesh instead. bed_soak Off C5_MISC_BED_SOAK_ON / _OFF Waits at bed temperature before a fresh mesh (bed_soak_minutes, 2 by default), so the plate stops warping first. Skipped below 45 °C. clog_detection Off SET_PIN PIN=clog_detection Pauses the print when a tool's filament wheel stops turning while filament is loaded. If you get false positives, turn it off. lower_bed_on_end Off C5_MISC_LOWER_BED_ON_END_ON / _OFF Lowers the bed to the bottom after the print, so the plate is easy to take out. chamber_wait Off C5_MISC_CHAMBER_WAIT_ON / _OFF On: M191 waits for the chamber to reach temperature. Off: it sets the target and the print carries on while the chamber heats. door_notify Off C5_MISC_DOOR_NOTIFY_ON / _OFF Shows a pop-up (GrumpyScreen) and beeps when a door is opened during a print, or a print starts with one open. quiet_mode Off C5_MISC_QUIET_MODE_ON / _OFF Silences the buzzer for anything it uses (start / end tune, door, etc). chamber_heat_fan_full (Pro) Off C5_MISC_CHAMBER_HEAT_FAN_FULL_ON / _OFF Keeps the chamber heater fan at 90% while the chamber heats, instead of slowing it near the target. host_pressure_advance (PA BRANCH ONLY INDEV) Off C5_MISC_HOST_PRESSURE_ADVANCE_ON / _OFF Runs the host pressure advance test at print start, see Printer Features.

items.title: For one print only
items.text:
A switch applies to every print until you change it. To change print start for a single job, add the setting to C5_PRINT_START in the slicer's start G-code instead. A value there wins over the switch for that print only.

Parameter Overrides FLOW_CALIBRATION=0 or 1 flow_calibration PURGE=0 or 1 purge PURGE_LINE=0 or 1 purge_line PURGE_LINE_ALL_TOOLS=0 or 1 purge_line_all_tools BED_LEVELING=0 or 1 bed_leveling HOST_PRESSURE_ADVANCE=0 or 1 host_pressure_advance BUILDPLATE_CHECK=0 Skips the build plate check (no switch)

For example, a print with no bucket purge and no purge line:

C5_PRINT_START TOOL=0 BED=60 HOTEND=220 PURGE=0 PURGE_LINE=0

Note

Putting C5_PRINT_START in the start G-code replaces the one OpenCreator builds for you, which fills in each tool's material, the used tools and the idle temperatures from the file. Leave it out unless you need a per-print override, see Slicer Configuration.

items.title: Changing the defaults
items.text: A switch's default is only used until you change it the first time. The defaults are in printer.creator5.cfg (purge_default, purge_line_default, bed_soak_default and so on). The current values are saved in c5_misc_variables.cfg in the config folder. You shouldn't be changing default values as it is just as easy as flicking a single switch.

items.title: VFA compensation
items.text:
VFA (vertical fine artifacts) are fine, evenly spaced vertical lines on printed walls. They come from small ripples in how the X and Y motors turn. At certain speeds a ripple matches the frame's resonance and shakes the toolhead enough to show on the print.

The Creator 5's mainboard drives its motors through FlashForge's MCLib motor library, which can cancel these ripples. It adds a small opposite ripple to each motor's current. Three ripples are corrected per motor: once, twice and four times per motor cycle (td1, td2 and td4). Each has an amplitude and two phases, one per direction of travel. Calibration measures those numbers with the toolhead's accelerometer.

items.title: On the stock firmware
items.text:
The VFA button on the stock touchscreen sends:

  1. G1 Z100, then G1 X130 Y130: the bed down and the head to the middle.
  2. STEPPER_RESONANCE_FACTORY_CALIBRATE, a macro in the stock printer.vibration.cfg.

That macro turns all compensation off, then calibrates X and Y with STEPPER_RESONANCE_SEARCH_CALIBRATE. For each ripple and each direction, the search:

  • moves the head back and forth along one motor's axis at the speed where that ripple should hit the resonance, worked out from a fixed 200 Hz (stepper_x_freq / stepper_y_freq). The macro's step that would measure the real frequency is commented out.
  • measures the vibration with no compensation, then probes four phases, then finer phases, then amplitudes, and settles on the best phase and amplitude. Each measurement is about 0.6 s from the middle of one move.
  • uses the larger of the two directions' amplitudes, because the motor has one amplitude for both.

The results are sent to the motors straight away. The macro's SAVE_CONFIG is commented out, and the stock touchscreen doesn't send one with it, so as far as we can tell the results last until the next restart. After that the factory-calibrated values in printer.cfg come back.

The stock config also has a STEPPER_RESONANCE_DAMP_ENABLE macro, but it sets fixed numbers rather than calibrated ones: X off, and one hard-coded set for Y. Anything that ran it would replace a calibration's results with those.

The calibration also doesn't check that its result is better than no compensation. It leaves the printer's acceleration at the test's 5000 mm/s², and the analysis code crashes if the accelerometer gives no usable data five times in a row.

items.title: On OpenCreator
items.text:
Run VFA from the touchscreen or Fluidd's Calibrations group, or send VFA_COMPENSATION in the console. VFA + Graphs (VFA_COMPENSATION_GRAPH) does the same and draws graphs too (see below). Both are loud, and take a while. Add AXIS=X or AXIS=Y to redo just one motor; the other keeps its values.

  1. Safety checks. It refuses during a print, and unless all four heads are docked.
  2. Homes, and picks up T0. The head carries the accelerometer, and calibrating with a tool on matches the weight it prints with. Then G1 Z100 and G1 X130 Y130, as on stock.
  3. Finds each motor's real resonance. With compensation off, the head makes test moves from 20 to 300 mm/s, each about 8% faster than the last, then finer steps around the three strongest high points (a narrow peak can fall between two speeds). Where the main ripple peaks gives the motor's resonances: clear peaks, inside the swept speeds and at least 1.5 times the typical level. With no clear peak it uses the configured frequency (200 Hz unless saved) and says so.
  4. Picks the best resonance. With two strong ones, it calibrates at each, sweeps the speeds again with each result in both directions, and keeps whichever leaves less vibration. The strongest peak isn't always best, because the best setting depends on the speed it's tuned at. On one C5, the X motor tuned at its stronger 84 Hz resonance left 3 to 5 times more vibration from 30 to 120 mm/s than tuned at its 285 Hz one.
  5. Searches each ripple the same way stock does, with three differences:
    • Each measurement uses the whole steady-speed part of the move, found from the move's own timing, so there's less noise in every number it finds.
    • The two directions' amplitudes are combined into the one that gives the least vibration over both, not the larger of the two.
    • The result is measured again as it will run and compared with no compensation. A ripple that isn't at least 5% better is left off (amplitude 0) rather than saved.
  6. Puts things back. The printer's own acceleration settings are restored. If calibration stops with an error, the motors go back to their saved values instead of being left half-calibrated.
  7. Saves. SAVE_CONFIG writes the values and the measured frequencies to printer.cfg and restarts Klipper. With SAVE=0 nothing is written, but the new values are still used until Klipper restarts.

Every print start runs STEPPER_RESONANCE_DAMP_ENABLE. On OpenCreator that restores the calibrated values (MCLIB_APPLY_CALIBRATION), not fixed numbers.

A CSV of every measurement is written to /tmp/stepper_x_search_calibrate-<time>.csv (and stepper_y), for anyone who wants the raw numbers.

items.title: Graphs
items.text:
VFA + Graphs runs the same calibration, and measures the speeds again with compensation on. With two resonances it reuses the winner's check sweep, so there's nothing extra to measure. It draws one picture per motor to config/vfa/ (vfa_stepper_x.png, vfa_stepper_y.png), which you can open from Fluidd's or Mainsail's config files.

  • Top chart: how hard the toolhead shakes at each print speed, for each of the three ripples. Dotted lines are before compensation and solid lines after, so lower is better. Peaks are speeds where a ripple matches the frame's resonance, and a marker shows the speed each ripple was tuned at. A line that stops early is a ripple too fast there for the accelerometer to measure (over about 700 Hz): the 4x above about 100 mm/s and the 2x above about 200 mm/s. The 1x ripple, the one that matters at fast wall speeds, is shown up to 300 mm/s.
  • Bottom chart: each ripple at its worst speed, before and after, with how much less it shakes. A ripple that was left off because it didn't help is labelled as such.

It takes longer than VFA by one more sweep for each motor with only one resonance.

items.title: When to run it
items.text: Run it if you see VFA lines on your prints, and again after changing or re-tensioning belts, since that moves the resonance.

items.title: During a print
items.text:
Calibration only finds the numbers. The cancelling happens on the mainboard, inside each motor's own control:

  • At print start, STEPPER_RESONANCE_DAMP_ENABLE sends each motor's saved values to the mainboard: for each ripple (1x, 2x, 4x), an amplitude and two phases, one per direction. The same values are also sent when Klipper starts.
  • While the motor turns, the mainboard adjusts the motor's current about 20,000 times a second. On top of the normal current it adds a small extra current that rises and falls with the motor's position: once, twice and four times per motor cycle, timed with the phase for the direction it's turning, so it pushes against each ripple as it happens. It follows the motor's actual position, so it works at any speed and through speed changes, with nothing for Klipper to calculate per move. Prints aren't slowed down at all.
  • At high speed, the mainboard switches a motor to a separate high-speed control mode, which doesn't add the compensation. That happens at about 510 mm/s of belt travel: roughly 360 to 510 mm/s of toolhead speed, depending on the direction of travel. Walls at 300 mm/s are always compensated.
  • At print end, or when a print is cancelled, STEPPER_RESONANCE_DAMP_DISABLE turns it off. The next print start turns it back on.
  • With ripple correction, a ripple that has a ripple correction table (2x and 4x after RIPPLE_CALIBRATE) uses the table at the speeds it was calibrated for, and VFA above and below them.
